newsitem.title: USA: Iraq Kurds said to agree ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Iraq Kurds said to agree ceasefire.

text.p: The two Kurdish factions fighting in Northern Iraq have promised to observe a ceasefire from midnight on Wednesday, Iraq time, the U.S. State Department said on Wednesday.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the agreement followed contacts by the United States, Britain and Turkey with Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).

"Both parties have given commitments to begin the ceasefire at midnight tonight, October 23, Iraq time," Burns said in a statement. "We call on both parties to honour those commitments, to repeat them publicly, and to place their forces in defensive postures."

Burns noted that Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau, who held separate talks with the KDP and PUK in Turkey this week, had said in a statement on Wednesday morning that both factions agreed in principle to an immediate ceasefire.
"Fighting in the region continued last night, and the ceasefire did not take hold as expected," he said.
Burns' statement called on Iran and Iraq to avoid actions which could make the process of Kurdish reconciliation more difficult and worsen tensions in the region.
